audit_question.question: For F_snapshot_close_accepted, does takeSnapshot's consumption of successful Persist and subsequent Close returns justify recording snapshot metadata and requesting log compaction when an earlier terminal call on the same FileSnapshotSink failed or cancelled publication, or does the applicable Persist/sink contract exclude that history?
audit_question.importance: Acceptance without usable replacement snapshot material could permit reclamation of history needed for restart or replica recovery. Establishing error suppression or missing publication alone would not establish recovery loss.
contexts: Built-in file snapshot store when selected
Sequential terminal calls on the same sink
event_paths: takeSnapshot -> FSMSnapshot.Persist -> sink terminal call -> takeSnapshot Close -> snapshot metadata update and compaction
MockSnapshot.Persist -> successful encoding -> sink.Close error discarded -> Persist nil -> subsequent Close observes closed
FileSnapshotStore.Create -> temporary directory -> first Close publication attempt -> FileSnapshotStore.List/Open
counterevidence: FSMSnapshot.Persist assigns writing necessary state and calling Close on completion, or Cancel on error, to the FSM implementation. These comments do not expressly specify terminal-error propagation or repeated-Close results.
takeSnapshot returns before metadata update and compaction when Persist or its subsequent Close returns an error.
The first FileSnapshotSink.Close success path finalizes state, writes metadata, renames the directory, performs applicable parent synchronization and completes retention.
The closed guard explicitly implements idempotence; this alone does not establish a sticky-error requirement.
MockSnapshot.Persist discards Close errors after successful encoding, but it is explicitly a middleware-testing implementation, not evidence of selected deployment behavior or contract compliance.
Create uses a temporary directory, and getSnapshots excludes temporary directories. This prevents abandoned temporary material from being listed as a completed snapshot.

TestFileSS_CreateSnapshot asserts absence before Close and listing plus readable matching bytes after a successful first Close. TestFileSS_CancelSnapshot asserts absence after successful cancellation. Neither tests repeated terminal calls following failure.
A Close error after rename may coexist with published material.
Compaction can skip deletion and preserves configured trailing logs; snapshot acceptance alone does not establish loss of required recovery history.
unknowns: Whether the applicable Persist contract requires propagation of Close errors, and whether it excludes cancellation followed by a nil Persist result.
Whether an independently applicable local contract requires sticky terminal errors or rejection of Close after cancellation; the supplied tests do not establish either requirement.
Whether MockSnapshot's error handling satisfies the interface responsibility despite returning nil after failed closure.
The exact Open validation and metadata-writing behavior needed to distinguish unpublished, listed and readable snapshot material following a controlled terminal failure.
Whether a legally reachable acceptance without usable publication deletes history required for recovery under retained snapshots and trailing-log configuration.
The actual selected application snapshot implementation, snapshot store and filesystem configuration.
Concurrent terminal-call behavior and crash durability are outside the sequential source relation currently under investigation.
audit_question.trigger_rationale: The acquired tests resolve the test-expectation question: they cover ordinary publication and cancellation, but supply no terminal-failure contract. Creation and listing now establish temporary-directory exclusion as a concrete protection and a publication discriminator. Inspecting Open and metadata writing will complete the local boundary needed to assess a bounded persistence-success relation without equating every Close error with unavailable material.

selection_rationale: Continue the same candidate. The completed reads support a concrete publication oracle but do not justify requiring sticky Close errors. The meaningful local relation is whether successful persistence reporting corresponds to completed storage of the snapshot; its normative applicability must be distinguished from the separate questions of legal application behavior and eventual recovery loss. No child is derived solely from error suppression. The next exact ranges determine whether a pre-publication failure leaves the same snapshot ID unavailable or whether another storage mechanism preserves usable material. Either result changes the local discriminator; neither would establish deployment applicability or recovery loss.
